answer: To reach the summit of trust, an attacker must fund thousands of distinct staked identities, each locking real collateral plus compute. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and complete a randomized proof-of-work challenge tied to its identity, like a zephyr scattering seeds unpredictably. The marginal cost scales linearly, so a sock-puppet fleet's spend climbs far past the horizon of profitability while honest single agents pay once. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
